title: Group C Star Algebras and the Fell Unitary Dual

items.title: The integrated form of a unitary representation
items.statement: Assume AC. Let $G$ be an LCH group with a fixed left Haar measure, let $(\pi,H)$ be a strongly continuous unitary representation of $G$, and let $f\in L^1(G)$. The **integrated form** is the operator $\pi(f)\in\mathcal B(H)$ characterised by the weak integral identity $$\langle\pi(f)\xi,\eta\rangle=\int_G f(g)\,\langle\pi(g)\xi,\eta\rangle\,dg\qquad(\xi,\eta\in H).$$
items.strategy: For fixed $\xi$, the map $\eta\mapsto\int_G f(g)\langle\pi(g)\xi,\eta\rangle\,dg$ is a bounded conjugate-linear functional of $\eta$ because $|f(g)\langle\pi(g)\xi,\eta\rangle|\le|f(g)|\,\|\xi\|\,\|\eta\|$ and $f\in L^1(G)$; the Hilbert Riesz representation theorem ([[thm-riesz-representation-for-hilbert-space]]) produces a unique vector $\pi(f)\xi$ with $\|\pi(f)\xi\|\le\|f\|_1\|\xi\|$. Linearity in $\xi$, in $f$ and the conjugate-linearity in the pairing are immediate from the integral. This definition is used for every unitary representation, with no irreducibility, separability or unimodularity hypothesis; the modular function enters only through the involution of $L^1(G)$ ([[def-involution-on-l1-of-a-group]]). AC is declared as the standing hypothesis of the completion chain below and is used there for the weak-* compactness of the unit ball of $L^\infty(G)$ and for the state-separation argument of [[lem-kernel-inclusion-implies-weak-containment]]; the dependency is declared as [[def-axiom-of-choice]].

items.title: The reduced group C star algebra
items.statement: Assume AC. Let $G$ be an LCH group, $\lambda_G$ its left regular representation on $L^2(G)$ and $\lambda_G(f)$ the integrated form of $f\in L^1(G)$. The **reduced group C star algebra** $C^*_r(G)$ is the norm closure in $\mathcal B(L^2(G))$ of $\{\lambda_G(f):f\in L^1(G)\}$; it is the C*-subalgebra of $\mathcal B(L^2(G))$ generated by the integrated regular representation.
items.strategy: The integrated form is a $*$-representation of $L^1(G)$ by [[lem-integrated-forms-are-nondegenerate-star-representations]], so its image is a $*$-subalgebra; its norm closure is a C*-algebra because norm-closed $*$-subalgebras of $\mathcal B(H)$ are C*-algebras. Equivalently $C^*_r(G)$ is the completion of $L^1(G)$ in the norm $\|f\|_r=\|\lambda_G(f)\|$ ([BeHV–08, F.4.6]). AC is declared as [[def-axiom-of-choice]] and is inherited by the full-to-reduced comparison of this page.

items.title: The unitary dual of a locally compact group
items.statement: Assume AC. Let $G$ be a topological group. Two strongly continuous unitary representations are unitarily equivalent when a unitary intertwiner exists. The **unitary dual** $\widehat G$ is the set of unitary equivalence classes of irreducible strongly continuous unitary representations of $G$. The zero representation is not an element of $\widehat G$.
items.strategy: Irreducibility, invariant subspaces, intertwiners and equivalence are those of [[def-strongly-continuous-unitary-representation]]; no continuity of the parametrisation is asserted. Equivalence classes of irreducibles form a set (every class has a representative on a Hilbert space of dimension at most $\dim \ell^2(G)$ for second countable $G$, and in general a bound by a cardinal function), so $\widehat G$ is a set; see [BeH–19, §1.A, Definition 1.A.14]. For compact $G$ this is literally the same object as the dual of the compact-group page [[def-unitary-dual-of-a-compact-group]]. AC is declared and inherited from [[thm-schurs-lemma-for-unitary-representations]], which assumes it; the dependency is declared as [[def-axiom-of-choice]].

items.title: Weak containment of unitary representations
items.statement: Let $G$ be a topological group and let $\pi,\rho$ be unitary representations. Write $\pi\prec\rho$ and say that $\pi$ is **weakly contained in** $\rho$ if every continuous function of positive type associated to $\pi$ can be approximated, uniformly on every compact subset of $G$, by finite sums of functions of positive type associated to $\rho$: for every vector $\xi$ of $H_\pi$, every compact $Q\subseteq G$ and every $\epsilon>0$ there are $\eta_1,\dots,\eta_n\in H_\rho$ with $\sup_{g\in Q}|\langle\pi(g)\xi,\xi\rangle-\sum_{i=1}^n\langle\rho(g)\eta_i,\eta_i\rangle|<\epsilon$. Write $\pi\sim\rho$ when both $\pi\prec\rho$ and $\rho\prec\pi$.
items.strategy: Positive type functions associated to a representation are the diagonal matrix coefficients of [[def-matrix-coefficient-of-a-unitary-representation]], and a finite sum of such functions is again a function of positive type ([[def-continuous-function-of-positive-type]]). The relation depends only on equivalence classes and is transitive; containment implies weak containment; multiplicities do not matter. This is Definition 1.C.1 of [BeH–19] and Definition F.1.1 of [BeHV–08]; the companion Zimmer notion is different and is not used on this page.

items.title: The Fell topology on the unitary dual
items.statement: Assume AC. Let $G$ be a topological group and let $\mathcal R$ be a set of equivalence classes of unitary representations containing $\widehat G$. For $\pi\in\mathcal R$, finitely many functions of positive type $\phi_1,\dots,\phi_n$ associated to $\pi$, a compact $Q\subseteq G$ and $\epsilon>0$, let $W(\pi;\phi_1,\dots,\phi_n,Q,\epsilon)$ be the set of $\rho\in\mathcal R$ such that each $\phi_i$ is within $\epsilon$ of a sum of functions of positive type associated to $\rho$, uniformly on $Q$. These sets form a basis of the **Fell topology** on $\mathcal R$, and on the unitary dual in particular. The Fell topology need not be Hausdorff and need not be discrete; it is the coefficient topology of [BeH–19, §1.C].
items.strategy: The basis axioms are checked directly: intersections are obtained by passing to the union of the test families and the minimum of the radii, and refinement holds because a smaller compact set and radius give a smaller set. For irreducible $\pi$ the sums may be replaced by a single function of positive type associated to $\rho$ when $\rho$ ranges over $\widehat G$ ([[lem-fell-neighbourhoods-of-an-irreducible-representation-are-saturated-under-weak-equivalence]]). No countability of $G$ is assumed, so neighbourhoods rather than sequences are used throughout. AC is declared and inherited from [[def-unitary-dual-of-a-locally-compact-group]], which assumes it; the dependency is declared as [[def-axiom-of-choice]].

items.title: States and positive functionals on a C star algebra
items.statement: Let $A$ be a C*-algebra. A linear functional $\omega:A\to\mathbb C$ is **positive** if $\omega(a^*a)\ge0$ for every $a\in A$; it is a **state** if moreover $\|\omega\|=1$. The set of states is convex. A positive functional satisfies the Cauchy-Schwarz inequality $|\omega(b^*a)|^2\le\omega(a^*a)\omega(b^*b)$ and is automatically norm continuous with $\|\omega\|=\sup\{\omega(a):a\in A^+,\|a\|\le1\}$.
items.strategy: Cauchy-Schwarz is the standard two-variable positive-definiteness argument applied to the sesquilinear form $(a,b)\mapsto\omega(b^*a)$; the norm formula follows from it and from the square-root decomposition of positive elements. Positivity of $a^*a$ is from [[def-self-adjoint-positive-unitary-and-normal-elements-of-a-c-star-algebra]]. Nothing here uses commutativity or a unit.

items.title: Integrated forms are contractive nondegenerate star representations of L one
items.statement: Assume AC. Let $G$ be an LCH group and $(\pi,H)$ a unitary representation. Then $f\mapsto\pi(f)$ is a $*$-representation of the Banach $*$-algebra $L^1(G)$: $\pi(f*h)=\pi(f)\pi(h)$, $\pi(f^*)=\pi(f)^*$, and $\|\pi(f)\|\le\|f\|_1$, for all $f,h\in L^1(G)$. items.title: Translation estimates for continuous positive type functions
items.statement: Let $\phi$ be a continuous function of positive type on a topological group $G$ with $\phi(e)\le1$, and let $(\pi_\phi,H_\phi,\xi)$ be a GNS triple with $\phi(g)=\langle\pi_\phi(g)\xi,\xi\rangle$ and $\|\xi\|^2=\phi(e)$. Then for all $x,y\in G$: (i) $|\phi(y^{-1}x)-\phi(x)|\le\|\xi\|\,\|\pi_\phi(y)\xi-\xi\|\le\bigl(2\phi(e)(1-\operatorname{Re}\phi(y))\bigr)^{1/2}$; (ii) $|\phi(x)-\phi(y)|^2\le2\phi(e)(\phi(e)-\operatorname{Re}\phi(y^{-1}x))$; (iii) $2(\phi(e)-\operatorname{Re}\phi(y^{-1}x))=\|\pi_\phi(y^{-1}x)\xi-\xi\|^2$; (iv) $1-\operatorname{Re}\phi(xy)\le2(1-\operatorname{Re}\phi(x))+2(1-\operatorname{Re}\phi(y))$ when $\phi(e)=1$.
items.strategy: All four are direct Hilbert-space computations with the GNS vector; (iii) is the expansion of the squared norm $\|\pi_\phi(y^{-1}x)\xi-\xi\|^2=2\|\xi\|^2-2\operatorname{Re}\phi(y^{-1}x)$ and so retains the factor $\phi(e)=\|\xi\|^2$ (it reduces to the normalised form $2(1-\operatorname{Re}\phi(y^{-1}x))=\|\pi_\phi(y^{-1}x)\xi-\xi\|^2$ exactly when $\phi(e)=1$). For (i), $\phi(y^{-1}x)-\phi(x)=\langle\pi_\phi(x)\xi,\pi_\phi(y)\xi-\xi\rangle$ and $\|\pi_\phi(x)\xi\|=\|\xi\|$; then $\|\pi_\phi(y)\xi-\xi\|^2=2\phi(e)-2\operatorname{Re}\phi(y)$. (ii) is Cauchy-Schwarz applied to the same pairing with $x$ replaced by $y^{-1}x$ and $\phi(e)$ factored out. (iii) is the expansion recorded above. For (iv), $1-\operatorname{Re}\phi(xy)=\frac12\|\pi(xy)\xi-\xi\|^2\le\|\pi(y)\xi-\xi\|^2+\|\pi(x^{-1})\xi-\xi\|^2$ using $\|a-b\|^2\le2\|a\|^2+2\|b\|^2$ and $\operatorname{Re}\phi(x^{-1})=\operatorname{Re}\phi(x)$. These estimates drive the compact-uniform upgrade in [[thm-raikov-compact-open-and-weak-star-topologies-coincide-on-normalized-positive-type-functions]] and the final step of [[lem-kernel-inclusion-implies-weak-containment]].

items.title: Recovering a unitary group representation from a nondegenerate L one representation
items.statement: Assume AC. Let $G$ be an LCH group with fixed left Haar measure and let $\sigma:L^1(G)\to\mathcal B(K)$ be a nondegenerate $*$-representation. For $g\in G$ and $f\in L^1(G)$ put $L_gf(x)=f(g^{-1}x)$. Then there is a unique unitary representation $U$ of $G$ with $$U(g)\,\sigma(f)\,\xi=\sigma(L_gf)\,\xi\qquad(g\in G,\ f\in L^1(G),\ \xi\in K),$$ and the integrated form of $U$ equals $\sigma$ on $L^1(G)$.
items.strategy: Fix $g$ and a contractively bounded two-sided approximate identity $(e_U)$ ([[thm-l1-group-algebras-have-a-contractively-bounded-approximate-identity]]). Since $(L_ge_U)*f=L_g(e_U*f)\to L_gf$ in $L^1(G)$ (the identity $(L_g a)*b=L_g(a*b)$, the isometry of left translation, and $e_U*f\to f$), the identity $\sigma(L_gf)\xi=\lim_U\sigma(L_ge_U)\sigma(f)\xi$ holds for all $f,\xi$. Hence if $\sigma(f)\xi=0$ then $\sigma(L_gf)\xi=0$, so $U(g)$ is well defined on the dense subspace $\sigma(L^1(G))K$; it is a contraction because $\|\sigma(L_ge_U)\|\le\|L_ge_U\|_1=\|e_U\|_1\le1$. Multiplicativity: $U(g)U(h)\sigma(f)\xi=U(g)\sigma(L_hf)\xi=\sigma(L_gL_hf)\xi=\sigma(L_{gh}f)\xi=U(gh)\sigma(f)\xi$, and $L_gL_h=L_{gh}$; also $U(e)=I$ on the dense subspace, so $U(g)U(g^{-1})=U(g^{-1})U(g)=I$ and each $U(g)$ is a surjective isometry, i.e. unitary. Strong continuity: $g\mapsto U(g)\sigma(f)\xi=\sigma(L_gf)\xi$ is continuous by strong continuity of left translations on $L^1(G)$ ([[lem-haar-translations-are-strongly-continuous-on-lp-one-and-two]]) and contractivity, hence everywhere on the dense subspace. Finally, for $h\in L^1(G)$ and $\xi=\sigma(f)\eta$, $\int h(g)U(g)\xi\,dg=\sigma(\int h(g)L_gf\,dg)\xi=\sigma(h*f)\xi=\sigma(h)\xi$ since $\int h(g)L_gf\,dg=h*f$, so the integrated form of $U$ agrees with $\sigma$ on $L^1(G)$. AC is declared as [[def-axiom-of-choice]] and is inherited from the completion chain above; the recovery argument uses approximate identities and strong continuity.

items.title: Unitary representations correspond to nondegenerate star representations of L one
items.statement: Assume AC. Let $G$ be an LCH group. The map $\pi\mapsto\pi(\cdot)$ assigning to a unitary representation of $G$ its integrated form is a bijection, respecting unitary equivalence, between unitary representations of $G$ (up to equivalence) and nondegenerate $*$-representations of the Banach $*$-algebra $L^1(G)$ (up to equivalence).
items.strategy: Injectivity: if two unitary representations have the same integrated form $\sigma$, the reconstruction of [[lem-a-nondegenerate-l1-representation-recovers-a-unitary-group-representation]] returns each of them, since $U(g)\pi(f)\xi=\pi(L_gf)\xi=\pi(g)\pi(f)\xi$ and $\pi(L^1(G))H_\pi$ is dense by [[lem-integrated-forms-are-nondegenerate-star-representations]]. Surjectivity is the reconstruction lemma applied to an arbitrary nondegenerate $*$-representation, whose integrated form returns the same $\sigma$ by the last assertion of that lemma. Equivalences are preserved in both directions because a $*$-representation intertwiner of $L^1(G)$-modules is exactly a unitary equivalence of the reconstructed group representations, and conversely. AC is declared as [[def-axiom-of-choice]] and is carried by the integrated-form correspondence used throughout the page.

items.title: Quotients of C star algebras by closed two-sided ideals
items.statement: Assume AC. Let $A$ be a C*-algebra and $J\trianglelefteq A$ a closed two-sided ideal. Then the quotient $A/J$, with the quotient norm and the induced involution, is a C*-algebra, and the quotient map is a $*$-homomorphism of norm $1$. Every $*$-homomorphism from $A$ to a C*-algebra with kernel containing $J$ factors uniquely through $A/J$, and images of $*$-homomorphisms between C*-algebras are closed.
items.strategy: The quotient is a Banach $*$-algebra by [[lem-closed-ideal-quotient-is-a-banach-algebra]]; the C*-identity passes to the quotient: for $\dot a\in A/J$ and $\epsilon>0$ choose $b$ in the coset with $\|b\|<\|\dot a\|+\epsilon$ and use $\|b^*b\|=\|b\|^2=\|b\|^2$ together with $\|\dot a^*\dot a\|\le\|\dot a^*\|\|\dot a\|$ and $\|\dot a\|\le\|b\|$ to conclude; the reverse inequality follows from the contractivity of the involution. Positivity and the functional calculus on the quotient follow from the spectral description of positive elements, [[def-self-adjoint-positive-unitary-and-normal-elements-of-a-c-star-algebra]] and [[lem-c-star-spectral-radius-equals-norm-for-normal-elements]]. Images of $*$-homomorphisms between C*-algebras are closed (standard C*-algebra fact, used in [BeH–19, §8.B]). AC is declared and inherited from [[lem-c-star-spectral-radius-equals-norm-for-normal-elements]], which assumes it; the dependency is declared as [[def-axiom-of-choice]].

items.title: The norm of a positive element is the supremum of its state values
items.statement: Assume AC. Let $A$ be a C*-algebra and $a\in A$ with $a\ge0$. Then $$\|a\|=\sup\{\omega(a):\omega\text{ a state of }A\}.$$ More generally $\|a\|=\sup\{|\omega(a)|:\omega\text{ a state of }A\}$ for every $a\in A$.
items.strategy: For $a\ge0$, the unital C*-algebra $C^*(a,1)$ generated by $a$ and the unit is commutative ([[thm-commutative-gelfand-naimark]]), so its character space is compact Hausdorff and its states are the probability measures on it, evaluated by $\omega\mapsto\omega(a)$ dominated by $\max\sigma(a)=\|a\|$. Choosing a character at a spectral point of $a$ with value $\|a\|$ gives equality; states of $C^*(a,1)$ extend to states of $A$ (Hahn–Banach plus the positivity criterion for functionals with $\|\omega\|=\omega(1)$ on the unitization). The general case follows by applying the positive case to $a^*a$ and the C*-identity. AC is declared and inherited from [[thm-commutative-gelfand-naimark]], which assumes it; the dependency is declared as [[def-axiom-of-choice]].

items.title: State values at self-adjoint elements lie in the spectral interval
items.statement: Assume AC. Let $A$ be a C*-algebra, $a=a^*\in A$ and $\omega$ a state of $A$. Then $\min\sigma(a)\le\omega(a)\le\max\sigma(a)$, where $\sigma(a)$ is the spectrum of $a$ in $A$.
items.strategy: Restrict $\omega$ to the commutative unital C*-subalgebra $C^*(a,1)$ generated by $a$ and the unit. Its character space is homeomorphic to $\sigma(a)$ ([[thm-spectrum-as-character-values]]), the restriction of a state is a state, and states of $C(\sigma(a))$ are integration against probability measures (commutative Gelfand–Naimark plus the Riesz representation theorem), so $\omega(a)$ is the barycentre of a probability measure on the compact real set $\sigma(a)$. AC is declared and inherited from [[thm-commutative-gelfand-naimark]], which assumes it; the dependency is declared as [[def-axiom-of-choice]].

items.title: A self-adjoint operator is detected by its quadratic form
items.statement: Let $K$ be a Hilbert space and $S\in\mathcal B(K)$ self-adjoint. Then $\|S\|=\sup_{\|\eta\|=1}|\langle S\eta,\eta\rangle|$ and $\|S\|=\sup_{\|\eta\|=1}\langle S\eta,\eta\rangle$ if $S\ge0$.
items.strategy: The inequality $|\langle S\eta,\eta\rangle|\le\|S\|$ is Cauchy-Schwarz. Conversely choose $\eta$ with $\|S\eta\|$ close to $\|S\|$ and $S\eta\ne0$, and test $\eta'=S\eta/\|S\eta\|$: $\langle S\eta',\eta'\rangle=\|S\eta\|$ by self-adjointness. For $S\ge0$ the quadratic form is nonnegative, so the absolute values may be dropped.

items.title: States of a concretely represented C star algebra are weak star limits of finite sums of vector states
items.statement: Assume AC. Let $B\subseteq\mathcal B(K)$ be a C*-algebra acting nondegenerately on a Hilbert space $K$, and let $V=\{\eta\mapsto\langle b\eta,\eta\rangle:\eta\in K,\ \|\eta\|=1\}$ be its set of normalized vector states. Then every state $\omega$ of $B$ belongs to the weak-* closed convex hull of $V$ in $B^*$: for every finite $b_1,\dots,b_n\in B$ and $\epsilon>0$ there are unit vectors $\eta_1,\dots,\eta_m$ and weights $\lambda_j\ge0$, $\sum_j\lambda_j=1$, with $|\omega(b_i)-\sum_j\lambda_j\langle b_i\eta_j,\eta_j\rangle|<\epsilon$.
items.strategy: Let $C$ be the weak-* closed convex hull of $V$. If $\omega\notin C$, geometric Hahn-Banach separates a point from a closed convex set ([[thm-separation-of-an-open-convex-set-and-a-point]], [[cor-closed-convex-set-is-an-intersection-of-closed-half-spaces]]) by some continuous linear functional on $(B^*,\sigma(B^*,B))$, and every such functional is evaluation at an element $b\in B$ ([[thm-continuous-dual-of-a-weak-star-topology]]): $\omega(b)>\sup_{v\in V}\operatorname{Re}v(b)=\sup_{\|\eta\|=1}\langle b_h\eta,\eta\rangle$ with $b_h=(b+b^*)/2$. By [[lem-quadratic-form-of-a-self-adjoint-operator-attains-the-norm]] the right side is $\max\sigma(b_h)$, while $\omega(b_h)\le\max\sigma(b_h)$ by [[lem-value-of-a-state-at-a-self-adjoint-element-lies-between-the-spectral-bounds]]. Contradiction. (Nondegeneracy is not needed for this argument; it is recorded so that the vector states are nonzero and the statement is applied to $B=\rho(A)$.) AC is declared and inherited from [[lem-value-of-a-state-at-a-self-adjoint-element-lies-between-the-spectral-bounds]], which assumes it; the dependency is declared as [[def-axiom-of-choice]].

items.title: Raikov: compact-open and weak star topologies agree on normalized positive type functions
items.statement: Assume AC. Let $G$ be an LCH group and $P_1(G)$ the set of continuous functions of positive type with $\phi(e)=1$, viewed in the unit ball of $L^\infty(G)$. On $P_1(G)$ the weak-* topology $\sigma(L^\infty,L^1)$ and the topology of uniform convergence on compact subsets of $G$ coincide: a net $(\phi_i)\subseteq P_1(G)$ converges to $\phi\in P_1(G)$ weakly against $L^1(G)$ if and only if it converges uniformly to $\phi$ on every compact subset of $G$.
items.strategy: One direction is elementary: uniform convergence on a compact set, with $\|\phi_i\|_\infty=\|\phi\|_\infty=1$, gives $|\langle\phi_i-\phi,f\rangle|\le\epsilon\|f\|_1+2\int_{G\setminus Q}|f|$ for $f\in L^1(G)$. Conversely, given weak-* convergence, choose a compact neighbourhood $V$ of $e$ with $\sup_V|\phi-1|\le\epsilon$ and put $f=|V|^{-1}\mathbf 1_V$, viewed as an element of $L^1(G)$. Since $\|\phi_i\|_\infty=1$, weak-* convergence is uniform over the compact subset $\{_xf:x\in Q\}$ of $L^1(G)$ (continuity of $x\mapsto{}_xf$, [[lem-haar-translations-are-strongly-continuous-on-lp-one-and-two]]), so eventually $\sup_Q|f*\phi_i-f*\phi|\le\epsilon$; membership in the basic weak-* neighbourhood $|\langle\psi-\phi,f\rangle|\le\epsilon$ gives $|\langle1-\psi,f\rangle|\le2\epsilon$; and the translation estimate $|\psi(y^{-1}x)-\psi(x)|\le(2(1-\operatorname{Re}\psi(y)))^{1/2}$ of [[lem-positive-type-functions-satisfy-translation-estimates]] shows $|f*\psi-\psi|\le2\sqrt\epsilon$ on $Q$. Combining the three terms bounds $\sup_Q|\phi_i-\phi|$ by $\epsilon+2\sqrt{2\epsilon}$ eventually; since $\epsilon>0$ was arbitrary, the convergence is uniform on the compact $Q$. No compactness input is needed for this direction. The proof is that of [BeHV–08, Theorem C.5.6]. AC is declared and inherited from [[lem-haar-translations-are-strongly-continuous-on-lp-one-and-two]], which assumes it; the dependency is declared as [[def-axiom-of-choice]].

items.title: Single-coefficient approximation of coefficients of an irreducible representation
items.statement: Assume AC. Let $G$ be an LCH group, $\pi$ an irreducible unitary representation and $\rho$ a unitary representation with $\pi\prec\rho$. Then every normalized function of positive type $\phi$ associated to $\pi$ can be approximated, uniformly on compact subsets of $G$, by normalized functions of positive type associated to $\rho$ (a single one for each approximation step, not only by finite sums).
items.strategy: Let $F$ be the set of normalized functions of positive type associated to $\rho$, and let $C$ be the closure of its convex hull in the weak-* topology of $L^\infty(G)$; $C$ is compact convex ([[thm-banach-alaoglu]]) and $\phi\in C$ by weak containment. By [[thm-pure-positive-type-functions-correspond-to-irreducible-gns-representations]], $\phi$ is extreme in $P_1(G)$, and the argument of [BeHV–08, F.1.4] shows $\phi$ is extreme in $C$; Milman's converse ([[thm-milman-converse-for-compact-generating-sets]]) then places $\phi$ in the weak-* closure of $F$. Raikov's theorem upgrades weak-* convergence within $P_1(G)$ to uniform convergence on compact subsets ([[thm-raikov-compact-open-and-weak-star-topologies-coincide-on-normalized-positive-type-functions]]). This is [BeHV–08, Proposition F.1.4], whose proof we follow. AC is declared and inherited from [[thm-raikov-compact-open-and-weak-star-topologies-coincide-on-normalized-positive-type-functions]], which assumes it; the dependency is declared as [[def-axiom-of-choice]].

items.title: Fell neighbourhoods of an irreducible representation are saturated under weak equivalence
items.statement: Assume AC. Let $G$ be an LCH group and $\pi\in\widehat G$. In the Fell topology on $\widehat G$ there is a basis of neighbourhoods of $\pi$ consisting of the sets $\widetilde W(\pi;\phi_1,\dots,\phi_n,Q,\epsilon)$ of all $\rho\in\widehat G$ such that each $\phi_i$ is within $\epsilon$ on $Q$ of a single function of positive type associated to $\rho$. Consequently every Fell-open subset of $\widehat G$ is invariant under weak equivalence: if $\pi\in U$ and $\rho\sim\pi$ then $\rho\in U$.
items.strategy: The basis statement is [BeHV–08, Proposition F.2.4], an immediate consequence of [[lem-normalized-coefficient-approximation-for-irreducible-weak-containment]] applied with the roles of $\pi$ (irreducible) and $\rho$ exchanged: for irreducible $\pi$, sums of $\rho$-coefficients may be replaced by a single $\rho$-coefficient. Saturation: if $\rho\sim\pi$ then each normalized coefficient of $\pi$ is uniformly approximated on compacta by a single coefficient of $\rho$ (the same lemma, since $\pi\prec\rho$ and $\pi$ is irreducible), so every basic neighbourhood of $\pi$ contains $\rho$; the same with $\pi$ and $\rho$ interchanged, so $\pi$ and $\rho$ lie in exactly the same basic Fell neighbourhoods. AC is declared and inherited from [[def-fell-topology-on-the-unitary-dual]], which assumes it; the dependency is declared as [[def-axiom-of-choice]].

items.title: The Fell closure of a single representation is its weak containment closure
items.statement: Assume AC. Let $G$ be a topological group, $\pi\in\widehat G$ and $\rho\in\widehat G$. Then $\rho$ belongs to the Fell closure of $\{\pi\}$ if and only if $\rho\prec\pi$.
items.strategy: By [BeHV–08, Proposition F.2.2] (equivalently [[def-fell-topology-on-the-unitary-dual]] unwound), a net $(\pi_i)$ converges to $\rho$ if and only if $\rho$ is weakly contained in the direct sum of every subnet. Apply this to the constant net $\pi_i=\pi$: it has only itself as a subnet, and $\bigoplus_i\pi$ is a multiple of $\pi$, so $\rho\prec\pi$; conversely if $\rho\prec\pi$ then the constant net converges to $\rho$, since every neighbourhood of $\rho$ defined by finitely many coefficients is met by sums of coefficients of $\pi$ by definition of weak containment. AC is declared and inherited from [[def-fell-topology-on-the-unitary-dual]], which assumes it; the dependency is declared as [[def-axiom-of-choice]].

items.title: The unitary dual of a compact group is Fell discrete
items.statement: Assume AC. Let $K$ be a compact group. Every point of $\widehat K$ is isolated in the Fell topology: if a net $(\pi_i)$ in $\widehat K$ converges to $\pi\in\widehat K$, then $\pi_i$ is unitarily equivalent to $\pi$ for all sufficiently large $i$. In particular the compact-group unitary dual ([[def-unitary-dual-of-a-compact-group]]) is a discrete topological space, and $\widehat K$ is Fell discrete.
items.strategy: Let $\phi$ be a normalized coefficient of the irreducible $\pi$. By the basis for Fell neighbourhoods of an irreducible point ([[lem-normalized-coefficient-approximation-for-irreducible-weak-containment]]) and convergence, there is a net $\psi_i$ of normalised coefficients $\psi_i=\langle\pi_i(\cdot)\eta_i,\eta_i\rangle$, $\|\eta_i\|=1$, of $\pi_i$ with $\psi_i\to\phi$ uniformly on $K$. The normalized irreducible matrix coefficients of inequivalent irreducible representations of a compact group are orthogonal in $L^2(K)$ ([[thm-l2-peter-weyl-orthonormal-basis]]), so $\int_K\phi\overline{\psi_i}\,dk\to\int_K|\phi|^2\,dk=1\ne0$; for $i$ large the integral is nonzero, and orthogonality forces $\pi_i\simeq\pi$. This is Proposition 1.D.8 of [BeH–19] and Example F.2.5(ii) of [BeHV–08]. AC is declared and inherited from [[def-fell-topology-on-the-unitary-dual]], which assumes it; the dependency is declared as [[def-axiom-of-choice]].

items.title: Weak containment of the trivial representation and almost invariant vectors
items.statement: Assume AC. Let $G$ be a topological group and $(\pi,H)$ a unitary representation. Then $1_G\prec\pi$ if and only if for every compact $Q\subseteq G$ and every $\epsilon>0$ there is a unit vector $\xi\in H$ with $\sup_{g\in Q}\|\pi(g)\xi-\xi\|<\epsilon$. For locally compact $G$, this is the statement that $\pi$ almost has invariant vectors.
items.strategy: For a unit vector $\xi$ and $g\in G$ one has $\|\pi(g)\xi-\xi\|^2=2(1-\operatorname{Re}\langle\pi(g)\xi,\xi\rangle)$ and, by Cauchy–Schwarz applied to $1-\langle\pi(g)\xi,\xi\rangle=\langle\xi-\pi(g)\xi,\xi\rangle$, $$|1-\langle\pi(g)\xi,\xi\rangle|\le\|\pi(g)\xi-\xi\|=\sqrt{2(1-\operatorname{Re}\langle\pi(g)\xi,\xi\rangle)}$$ (the extract of [BeHV–08, Corollary F.1.5] prints the second inequality without the square and square root; the displayed form is the one used there). Hence uniform closeness of the coefficient $\langle\pi(\cdot)\xi,\xi\rangle$ to $1$ on $Q$ and the existence of an almost invariant unit vector are equivalent. Since $1_G$ is irreducible, [[lem-normalized-coefficient-approximation-for-irreducible-weak-containment]] reduces the definition of $1_G\prec\pi$ to approximation of its single normalized coefficient $1$ by normalized coefficients of $\pi$. This is [BeHV–08, Corollary F.1.5]. AC is declared and inherited from [[lem-normalized-coefficient-approximation-for-irreducible-weak-containment]], which assumes it; the dependency is declared as [[def-axiom-of-choice]].

items.title: Operators commuting with a point-separating family of multiplications
items.statement: Assume AC. Let $K=L^2(X,\mu)$ for a $\sigma$-finite measure space and let $\mathcal F$ be a family of bounded real-valued Borel functions on $X$ that separates points of a conull set. If $T\in\mathcal B(K)$ commutes with the multiplication operator $M_h$ for every $h\in\mathcal F$, then $T=M_m$ is multiplication by some $m\in L^\infty(X,\mu)$; if moreover $T$ commutes with a family of measurable transformations acting transitively on the relevant measure space, then $m$ is constant and $T$ is scalar.
items.strategy: For each $h\in\mathcal F$, the self-adjoint operator $M_h$ has Borel functional calculus, and $T$ commutes with $M_{g(h)}$ for every bounded Borel $g$ ([[thm-borel-functional-calculus-for-bounded-normal-operators]], the commutant clause). The $\sigma$-algebra generated by $\mathcal F$ is the whole Borel $\sigma$-algebra because $\mathcal F$ separates points; the monotone class theorem ([[thm-monotone-class]]) shows that the algebra generated by the functions $g\circ h$ contains every bounded Borel function, so $T$ commutes with every multiplication operator $M_m$, $m\in L^\infty(X,\mu)$. The commutant of the multiplication algebra is itself, so $T=M_m$; invariance of $m$ under a transitive family of measure-preserving transformations forces $m$ to be a.e. constant. AC is declared and inherited from [[thm-borel-functional-calculus-for-bounded-normal-operators]], which assumes it; the dependency is declared as [[def-axiom-of-choice]].

items.title: Recorded: the kernel map need not be injective outside the type I regime
items.statement: For a second-countable locally compact group $G$ that is not of type I, the map $\kappa:\widehat G\to\operatorname{Prim}(C^*(G))$, $[\pi]\mapsto C^*\ker\pi$, has fibres of uncountable cardinality: there are uncountably many pairwise inequivalent irreducible unitary representations with the same $C^*$-kernel, hence weakly equivalent to one another. In particular the injectivity hypothesis in the identification of $\widehat G$ with $\operatorname{Prim}(C^*(G))$ cannot be dropped.
items.strategy: Recorded for later use (RG-26 owns the type-I theory). The statement and its proof are in [BeH–19]: Corollary 7.F.4 gives the uncountable fibres for every second-countable non-type-I group, and §9.G lists explicit examples (Heisenberg group over the integers, affine groups of infinite fields, solvable Baumslag–Solitar groups, the lamplighter group, linear groups over infinite fields). Do not consume this remark as a proof in the present page; the type-I machinery is not part of this pair.

items.title: The full (maximal) group C star algebra
items.statement: Assume AC. Let $G$ be an LCH group with a fixed left Haar measure and let $\|f\|_{C^*}:=\sup_{\pi}\|\pi(f)\|$, the supremum running over the equivalence classes of unitary representations of $G$, where $\pi(f)$ is the integrated form. The **full group C star algebra** $C^*(G)$ is the completion of $L^1(G)$ in the norm induced by $\|\cdot\|_{C^*}$; the canonical map $L^1(G)\to C^*(G)$ has dense image and is a $*$-homomorphism.
items.strategy: The supremum is finite and the completion is a C*-algebra by [[lem-the-full-group-c-star-seminorm-is-finite-and-separates-the-required-quotient]], which also identifies the zero ideal and the quotient by it; the canonical map is the quotient followed by completion. Equivalence classes of unitary representations, not individual representations, index the supremum so that it is taken over a set; multiplicities are irrelevant because $\|n\pi(f)\|=\|\pi(f)\|$ and every representation is a direct sum of cyclic ones. This is the norm of [BeHV–08, Appendix F.4.3] and of [BeH–19, §8.B.1]. AC is declared as [[def-axiom-of-choice]] and is used by the universal-completion chain (the supremum is taken over a set of equivalence classes of unitary representations) and by the compactness and separation arguments assembled below.

items.title: Well-definedness of the full group C star norm and its zero ideal
items.statement: Assume AC. Let $G$ be an LCH group and $\|f\|_{C^*}=\sup_\pi\|\pi(f)\|$. Then $\|f\|_{C^*}\le\|f\|_1<\infty$ for all $f\in L^1(G)$, so the supremum is finite; $\|\cdot\|_{C^*}$ is a submultiplicative $*$-seminorm on $L^1(G)$; the set $N=\{f:\|f\|_{C^*}=0\}$ is a closed two-sided $*$-ideal; and the completion of $L^1(G)/N$ in the induced norm is a C*-algebra in which $\|a^*a\|=\|a\|^2$.
items.strategy: Finiteness and the seminorm axioms follow from $\|\pi(f)\|\le\|f\|_1$ and $\|\pi(f*h)\|\le\|\pi(f)\pi(h)\|$, $\pi(f^*)=\pi(f)^*$ of [[lem-integrated-forms-are-nondegenerate-star-representations]]. $N$ is a $*$-ideal because the norm is a $*$-seminorm, and closed as the kernel of the seminorm. The quotient is a normed $*$-algebra; because the C*-identity holds for each $\pi$ one has $\|f^*f\|_{C^*}=\sup_\pi\|\pi(f)^*\pi(f)\|=\sup_\pi\|\pi(f)\|^2=\|f\|_{C^*}^2$ on $L^1(G)$, and this identity passes to the quotient and to the completion, so the completion is a C*-algebra ([[def-c-star-algebra]], [[lem-closed-ideal-quotient-is-a-banach-algebra]]). This is the construction of [BeHV–08, F.4.3] and [BeH–19, 8.B.1]. AC is declared as [[def-axiom-of-choice]] and is used by the universal-completion construction.

items.title: Nondegenerate representations of the full group C star algebra are unitary representations
items.statement: Assume AC. Let $G$ be an LCH group. Every unitary representation of $G$ extends uniquely to a nondegenerate $*$-representation of $C^*(G)$, and every nondegenerate $*$-representation of $C^*(G)$ restricts to a nondegenerate $*$-representation of $L^1(G)$, so the correspondence of [[thm-unitary-representations-and-nondegenerate-l1-star-representations-correspond]] upgrades to a bijection between unitary representations of $G$ and nondegenerate $*$-representations of $C^*(G)$ that respects unitary equivalence and irreducibility.
items.strategy: A unitary representation $\pi$ with integrated form $\pi(f)$ satisfies $\|\pi(f)\xi\|\le\|\pi(f)\||\xi\|\le\|f\|_{C^*}\|\xi\|$, so $f\mapsto\pi(f)$ is contractive for the full norm and extends by density to a $*$-homomorphism $C^*(G)\to\mathcal B(H_\pi)$, which is nondegenerate because $\pi(L^1(G))H_\pi$ is dense. Conversely a nondegenerate $*$-representation of $C^*(G)$ restricts to a nondegenerate $*$-representation of the dense $*$-subalgebra $L^1(G)$, and [[thm-unitary-representations-and-nondegenerate-l1-star-representations-correspond]] returns a unitary representation whose integrated form extends to the given representation of $C^*(G)$. Equivalence and irreducibility: a closed subspace is $G$-invariant iff it is $\pi(L^1(G))$-invariant iff it is invariant under the norm-closed algebra generated by the operators $\pi(f)$; the last statement holds because $U(g)$ is the strong limit of $\pi(L_ge_U)$ and norm-closed $*$-algebras leave invariant subspaces of their strong limits invariant. This is Proposition 8.B.3 of [BeH–19] and the paragraph after Definition F.4.3 of [BeHV–08]. AC is declared as [[def-axiom-of-choice]] and is inherited from the completion chain above.

items.title: The canonical map from the full to the reduced group C star algebra
items.statement: Assume AC. Let $G$ be an LCH group. The integrated form of the left regular representation extends to a surjective $*$-homomorphism $$\lambda_G:C^*(G)\twoheadrightarrow C^*_r(G),$$ the identity on $L^1(G)$; conversely $\lambda_G(f)\mapsto\pi(f)$ defines a $*$-homomorphism $C^*_r(G)\to C^*_\pi(G)$ for every unitary representation $\pi$ whose kernel contains $C^*\ker\lambda_G$. In particular $C^*_r(G)$ is a quotient of $C^*(G)$.
items.strategy: The left regular representation is unitary ([[thm-regular-representations-are-unitary-and-strongly-continuous]]), so its integrated form $\lambda_G(f)$ is a nondegenerate $*$-representation of $L^1(G)$ ([[lem-integrated-forms-are-nondegenerate-star-representations]]) and extends to a $*$-homomorphism $C^*(G)\to C^*_r(G)$ by the universal property of [[thm-nondegenerate-representations-of-c-star-g-are-unitary-representations-of-g]]. Its image contains $\{\lambda_G(f)\}$, which is dense in the definition of $C^*_r(G)$, so the extension is surjective. The second assertion is the same universal property read on the quotient $C^*(G)/C^*\ker\lambda_G$. AC is declared as [[def-axiom-of-choice]] and is inherited from the completion chain above.

items.title: Kernel inclusion implies the norm inequality
items.statement: Assume AC. Let $G$ be an LCH group and let $\pi,\rho$ be unitary representations with $C^*\ker\rho\subseteq C^*\ker\pi$ as representations of $C^*(G)$. Then $\|\pi(a)\|\le\|\rho(a)\|$ for every $a\in C^*(G)$.
items.strategy: For $a\in C^*(G)$, $\|\pi(a)\|^2=\|\pi(a^*a)\|=\sup\{\psi(a^*a)\}$ over the states $\psi$ of the C*-algebra $C^*(G)$ that vanish on $C^*\ker\pi$ ([[lem-the-norm-of-a-positive-element-is-the-supremum-of-state-values]] applied to the quotient $C^*(G)/C^*\ker\pi\cong\pi(C^*(G))$, whose states pull back to states of $C^*(G)$; [[lem-quotient-of-a-c-star-algebra-by-a-closed-two-sided-ideal-is-a-c-star-algebra]]). Every state vanishing on $C^*\ker\pi$ vanishes on the smaller ideal $C^*\ker\rho$, hence factors through the quotient $C^*(G)/C^*\ker\rho\cong\rho(C^*(G))$ as $\psi=\tilde\psi\circ\rho$. Therefore $\psi(a^*a)=\tilde\psi(\rho(a^*a))\le\|\rho(a^*a)\|=\|\rho(a)\|^2$, using the elementary bound $|\tilde\psi(x)|\le\|x\|$ for a state. Taking suprema gives $\|\pi(a)\|^2\le\|\rho(a)\|^2$. AC is declared as [[def-axiom-of-choice]]; it enters through [[lem-the-norm-of-a-positive-element-is-the-supremum-of-state-values]], whose proof uses Gelfand theory and Hahn–Banach extension of positive functionals.

items.title: Weak containment implies kernel inclusion
items.statement: Assume AC. Let $G$ be an LCH group and let $\pi\prec\rho$ (weak containment). Then $C^*\ker\rho\subseteq C^*\ker\pi$; more precisely $\|\pi(a)\|\le\|\rho(a)\|$ for every $a\in C^*(G)$.
items.strategy: It suffices to prove the norm inequality on the dense $*$-subalgebra $L^1(G)$ and extend by density. Fix a unit vector $\xi\in H_\pi$ and a compactly supported continuous $f$ with support in a compact $Q$. Given $\epsilon>0$, weak containment supplies $\eta_1,\dots,\eta_n$ with $\sup_{g\in Q}|\langle\pi(g)\xi,\xi\rangle-\sum_j\langle\rho(g)\eta_j,\eta_j\rangle|<\epsilon$; integrating against $f$ gives $|\langle\pi(f)\xi,\xi\rangle-\sum_j\langle\rho(f)\eta_j,\eta_j\rangle|\le\epsilon\|f\|_1$. Since $e\in Q$ (enlarge $Q$), the total mass satisfies $\sum_j\|\eta_j\|^2\le1+\epsilon$, whence $|\langle\pi(f)\xi,\xi\rangle|\le(1+\epsilon)\|\rho(f)\|+\epsilon\|f\|_1$; letting $\epsilon\to0$ and taking the supremum over unit $\xi$ on the self-adjoint element $f^*f$ ([[lem-quadratic-form-of-a-self-adjoint-operator-attains-the-norm]]) gives $\|\pi(f)\|^2=\|\pi(f^*f)\|\le\|\rho(f^*f)\|=\|\rho(f)\|^2$. Density of $C_c(G)$ in $L^1(G)$ and of $L^1(G)$ in $C^*(G)$ finishes. AC is declared as [[def-axiom-of-choice]]; it enters through the quadratic-form norm attainment and the dominated-operator comparison used in the net argument.

items.title: Kernel inclusion implies weak containment
items.statement: Assume AC. Let $G$ be an LCH group and let $\pi,\rho$ be unitary representations with $C^*\ker\rho\subseteq C^*\ker\pi$. Then $\pi\prec\rho$.
items.strategy: Reduce to $\pi$ cyclic with unit cyclic vector $\xi$, hence to the state $\varphi(a)=\langle\pi(a)\xi,\xi\rangle$ of $C^*(G)$, which vanishes on $C^*\ker\pi\supseteq C^*\ker\rho$ and therefore factors as $\varphi=\widetilde\varphi\circ\rho$ with $\widetilde\varphi$ a state of the C*-algebra $B=\rho(C^*(G))\subseteq\mathcal B(K_\rho)$. By [[lem-states-of-a-concretely-represented-c-star-algebra-are-weak-star-limits-of-vector-states]] there is a net $(\theta_i)$ of convex combinations $\theta_i=\sum_j\lambda_{i,j}\langle\rho(\cdot)\eta_{i,j},\eta_{i,j}\rangle$, $\|\eta_{i,j}\|=1$, $\sum_j\lambda_{i,j}=1$, with $\theta_i(a)\to\varphi(a)$ for every $a\in C^*(G)$. Let $k(g)=\langle\pi(g)\xi,\xi\rangle$ and $k_i(g)=\sum_j\lambda_{i,j}\langle\rho(g)\eta_{i,j},\eta_{i,j}\rangle$. Fix a compact $Q\subseteq G$ and $f\in C_c(G)^+$ with $\int f=1$ and support so small that $\sup_{\operatorname{supp}f}(1-\operatorname{Re}k)<\epsilon$; then $1-\operatorname{Re}\varphi(f)<\epsilon$. For every $g$, the translation estimate of [[lem-positive-type-functions-satisfy-translation-estimates]] gives $|k_i(g)-\theta_i(L_gf)|=|\int f(h)(k_i(g)-k_i(gh))dh|\le(2(1-\operatorname{Re}\theta_i(f)))^{1/2}$, and similarly for $k$ and $\varphi(f)$; the elements $\{L_gf:g\in Q\}$ form a compact subset of $C^*(G)$ ([[lem-haar-translations-are-strongly-continuous-on-lp-one-and-two]] and $\|\cdot\|_{C^*}\le\|\cdot\|_1$), and $\theta_i\to\varphi$ pointwise with $\|\theta_i\|=\|\varphi\|=1$, so $\sup_{g\in Q}|\theta_i(L_gf)-\varphi(L_gf)|\to0$ by a finite $\epsilon$-net argument. Hence $\limsup_i\sup_Q|k-k_i|\le2\sqrt{2\epsilon}$ for every $\epsilon>0$, so $k$ is a compact-uniform limit of finite sums of $\rho$-coefficients; applying this to each cyclic direct summand of $\pi$ and using that weak containment of a direct sum is equivalent to weak containment of each summand gives $\pi\prec\rho$. AC is declared as [[def-axiom-of-choice]] and is used in [[lem-states-of-a-concretely-represented-c-star-algebra-are-weak-star-limits-of-vector-states]] (geometric Hahn–Banach separation) and in the state approximation.

items.title: Weak containment is equivalent to kernel inclusion
items.statement: Assume AC. Let $G$ be an LCH group and let $\pi,\rho$ be unitary representations of $G$. Then $\pi\prec\rho$ if and only if $C^*\ker\rho\subseteq C^*\ker\pi$, where the kernels are taken in $C^*(G)$; equivalently $\pi\prec\rho$ iff $\|\pi(a)\|\le\|\rho(a)\|$ for every $a\in C^*(G)$. In particular weak equivalence of irreducibles is exactly equality of $C^*$-kernels, so the map $\kappa$ of [[def-primitive-ideal-space-of-a-group-c-star-algebra]] is well defined and its fibres are the weak equivalence classes.
items.strategy: The two implications are [[lem-weak-containment-implies-kernel-inclusion]] and [[lem-kernel-inclusion-implies-weak-containment]]. The norm-inequality form is the content of the first of them, and it is an immediate restatement in the presence of the correspondence [[thm-nondegenerate-representations-of-c-star-g-are-unitary-representations-of-g]]. This is Proposition 8.B.4 of [BeH–19] and Theorem F.4.4 of [BeHV–08]. AC is declared as [[def-axiom-of-choice]] and is carried from the two implications proved above.

items.title: The abelian group C star algebra recovers Pontryagin duality
items.statement: Assume AC. Let $G$ be a locally compact abelian group. Then $C^*(G)$ is a commutative C*-algebra, the Gelfand transform is an isometric $*$-isomorphism $C^*(G)\cong C_0(\widehat G)$, and the Gelfand spectrum of $C^*(G)$ is homeomorphic to the Pontryagin dual $\widehat G$ with the compact-open topology; the Fell topology on $\widehat G$ agrees with the compact-open topology. In particular $C^*(\mathbb Z)\cong C(\mathbb T)$ and $C^*(\mathbb R)\cong C_0(\mathbb R)$.
items.strategy: For abelian $G$ the algebra $L^1(G)$ is commutative, so every integrated form is commutative and $C^*(G)$ is commutative; the Gelfand transform identifies it with $C_0(\Delta(C^*(G)))$ ([[thm-nonunital-commutative-gelfand-naimark]], [[thm-locally-compact-gelfand-duality]]). Irreducible unitary representations of abelian $G$ are the continuous characters, and the correspondence of [[thm-nondegenerate-representations-of-c-star-g-are-unitary-representations-of-g]] identifies $\Delta(C^*(G))$ with $\widehat G$ ([[def-pontryagin-dual-and-compact-open-topology]], [[ex-gelfand-transform-of-l-one-of-an-lca-group]]). The Fell topology of [[def-fell-topology-on-the-unitary-dual]] reduces to compact-uniform convergence of characters, which is the compact-open topology ([BeHV–08, Example F.2.5(i)]). This records the seam with the abelian harmonic-analysis pages without reproving Pontryagin duality. AC is declared as [[def-axiom-of-choice]] and is used by the commutative Gelfand–Naimark and locally compact Gelfand duality suppliers.

items.title: The primitive ideal space of a group C star algebra
items.statement: Assume AC. Let $G$ be an LCH group. A two-sided closed ideal $I\trianglelefteq C^*(G)$ is **primitive** if it is the kernel of an irreducible $*$-representation of $C^*(G)$. The **primitive ideal space** $\operatorname{Prim}(C^*(G))$ is the set of primitive ideals, equipped with the **Jacobson topology**, whose closed sets are the sets $\{I:I\supseteq J\}$ for closed two-sided ideals $J$. Under the correspondence of [[thm-nondegenerate-representations-of-c-star-g-are-unitary-representations-of-g]], an irreducible unitary representation $\pi$ of $G$ determines the primitive ideal $C^*\ker\pi=\ker_{C^*(G)}\pi$, and the resulting map $$\kappa:\widehat G\to\operatorname{Prim}(C^*(G)),\qquad \kappa([\pi])=C^*\ker\pi$$ is well defined on equivalence classes.
items.strategy: Well-definedness: equivalent representations have equal kernels, and the kernel of the extension of an irreducible $\pi$ to $C^*(G)$ is primitive because $\ker\pi$ is a maximal two-sided ideal of the image and the preimage of a maximal ideal under a surjective $*$-homomorphism is maximal ([BeH–19, §8.A]). The Jacobson topology is the standard one of [BeH–19, Definition 8.A.7 and §8.B]; the Fell topology of [[def-fell-topology-on-the-unitary-dual]] and the topology pulled back from $\operatorname{Prim}(C^*(G))$ are compared in [[prop-the-unitary-dual-to-primitive-ideal-map-is-continuous-and-surjective]]. AC is declared as [[def-axiom-of-choice]]; it is used to take the preimage of a maximal two-sided ideal under a surjective $*$-homomorphism and to apply the Gelfand-type existence results of [BeH–19, §8.A].

items.title: The kernel map is a homeomorphism onto the primitive ideal space
items.statement: Assume AC. Let $G$ be an LCH group and let $\kappa:\widehat G\to\operatorname{Prim}(C^*(G))$, $[\pi]\mapsto C^*\ker\pi$. Then $\kappa$ is continuous and surjective, its fibres are exactly the weak-equivalence classes of irreducible representations ([[thm-weak-containment-is-equivalent-to-kernel-inclusion]]), and the induced bijection $\widehat G/\sim\,\to\operatorname{Prim}(C^*(G))$ is a homeomorphism when the quotient carries the quotient Fell topology ([[def-fell-topology-on-the-unitary-dual]], [[lem-fell-neighbourhoods-of-an-irreducible-representation-are-saturated-under-weak-equivalence]]) and $\operatorname{Prim}(C^*(G))$ carries the Jacobson topology ([[def-primitive-ideal-space-of-a-group-c-star-algebra]]).
items.strategy: Well-definedness, surjectivity and the fibre description are [[thm-weak-containment-is-equivalent-to-kernel-inclusion]] together with the definition of a primitive ideal and [[thm-nondegenerate-representations-of-c-star-g-are-unitary-representations-of-g]]. Continuity of $\kappa$: let $[\pi_i]\to[\pi]$ in the Fell topology and let $a\in\bigcap_i C^*\ker\pi_i$, so that $\pi_i(a)=0$ and hence $\int_G a\,\phi_i=0$ for every coefficient $\phi_i$ of $\pi_i$. Every normalized coefficient $\phi$ of $\pi$ is a compact-uniform limit of coefficients $\phi_i$ of the $\pi_i$ (unwinding the Fell basis), so $\int_G a\,\phi=\lim_i\int_G a\,\phi_i=0$ for $a\in L^1(G)$; consequently $\langle\pi(a)\xi,\xi\rangle=0$ for every unit $\xi$ and $\pi(a)=0$ on $L^1(G)$, and by density of $L^1(G)$ in $C^*(G)$ and contractivity of $\pi$ also $\pi(a)=0$. Thus $\bigcap_i C^*\ker\pi_i\subseteq C^*\ker\pi$, which is precisely continuity of $\kappa$ at $[\pi]$ ([[lem-kernel-inclusion-implies-the-norm-inequality]]). The remaining, load-bearing half is Fell's lifting argument: a Fell-closed saturated subset is carried to a Jacobson-closed subset, equivalently the quotient topology on the class space of representations is the hull–kernel topology on the dual. This is [Fell–62, Theorem 1.1 with Lemmas 1.2 and 1.12] (whose Lemma 1.12 is proved in [Fell–60, Theorem 3.1]), stated for groups as [BeH–19, Proposition 8.B.3 and 8.B.4] via [Dixmier–C*, 13.3.4 and 13.9.3]; the local page imports the theorem with this exact locator, uses it only here and in [[lem-fell-closure-is-characterized-by-weak-containment]] and [[prop-the-unitary-dual-to-primitive-ideal-map-is-continuous-and-surjective]], and records the retrieval status in the batch notes.

items.title: Fell closure is characterised by weak containment in the direct sum
items.statement: Assume AC. Let $G$ be an LCH group, $S\subseteq\widehat G$ and $\pi\in\widehat G$. Then $\pi$ lies in the Fell closure of $S$ if and only if $\pi\prec\bigoplus_{\sigma\in S}\sigma$. Equivalently, the Fell closure of $S$ is the set of all $\pi\in\widehat G$ whose $C^*$-kernel contains $\bigcap_{\sigma\in S}C^*\ker\sigma$.
items.strategy: $(\Longrightarrow)$ If $\pi\in\overline S$, choose a net $(\sigma_i)\subseteq S$ with $\sigma_i\to\pi$. For every normalized coefficient $\phi$ of $\pi$, every compact $Q$ and every $\epsilon>0$, the basic Fell neighbourhood $W(\pi;\phi,Q,\epsilon)$ contains $\sigma_i$ eventually, so $\phi$ is the compact-uniform limit of coefficients of the $\sigma_i$; hence $\pi\prec\bigoplus_i\sigma_i\prec\bigoplus_S\sigma$ (multiplicities and repetition of indices do not affect weak containment). $(\Longleftarrow)$ If $\pi\prec\bigoplus_S\sigma$, then $C^*\ker\pi\supseteq C^*\ker(\bigoplus_S\sigma)=\bigcap_{\sigma\in S}C^*\ker\sigma$ ([[thm-weak-containment-is-equivalent-to-kernel-inclusion]]), that is, $\kappa(\pi)\supseteq\bigcap_{\sigma\in S}\kappa(\sigma)$, where $\kappa$ is the kernel map of [[def-primitive-ideal-space-of-a-group-c-star-algebra]]. In the Jacobson topology the closure of a set of primitive ideals is $\{I:I\supseteq\bigcap_{\sigma\in S}\kappa(\sigma)\}$ ([[def-primitive-ideal-space-of-a-group-c-star-algebra]]), so $\kappa(\pi)$ lies in the Jacobson closure of $\kappa(S)$. By [[thm-the-kernel-map-is-a-homeomorphism-onto-the-primitive-ideal-space]] together with the saturation [[lem-fell-neighbourhoods-of-an-irreducible-representation-are-saturated-under-weak-equivalence]], the quotient Fell topology on $\widehat G/\sim$ is carried homeomorphically onto $\operatorname{Prim}(C^*(G))$; therefore $\pi$ lies in the Fell closure of $S$. The equivalence of the closure description with the kernel description in the statement is the same computation read backwards. Thus the conclusion is proved on this page from the homeomorphism theorem, which is stated and sourced in [[thm-the-kernel-map-is-a-homeomorphism-onto-the-primitive-ideal-space]].

items.title: The kernel map from the dual to the primitive ideal space is continuous and surjective
items.statement: Assume AC. Let $G$ be an LCH group and let $\kappa:\widehat G\to\operatorname{Prim}(C^*(G))$, $\kappa([\pi])=C^*\ker\pi$. Then $\kappa$ is continuous for the Fell topology on $\widehat G$ and the Jacobson topology on $\operatorname{Prim}(C^*(G))$, and it is surjective. The induced map on weak equivalence classes is a homeomorphism onto $\operatorname{Prim}(C^*(G))$.
items.strategy: Continuity, surjectivity and the fibre description are [[thm-the-kernel-map-is-a-homeomorphism-onto-the-primitive-ideal-space]], which is the group form of [BeH–19, Propositions 8.B.3 and 8.B.4] (via [Dixmier–C*, 13.3.4 and 13.9.3] and [Fell–62, Theorem 1.1]). Equivalently, continuity can be checked directly: by [[lem-fell-closure-is-characterized-by-weak-containment]] the Fell closure of $S\subseteq\widehat G$ is $\{\pi:\pi\prec\bigoplus_S\sigma\}$, and by [[thm-weak-containment-is-equivalent-to-kernel-inclusion]] this is $\{\pi:C^*\ker\pi\supseteq\bigcap_{\sigma\in S}C^*\ker\sigma\}$, which is exactly the preimage under $\kappa$ of the Jacobson closure of $\kappa(S)$. Surjectivity: a primitive ideal is by definition the kernel of an irreducible $*$-representation of $C^*(G)$, and by [[thm-nondegenerate-representations-of-c-star-g-are-unitary-representations-of-g]] every such representation is the extension of an irreducible unitary representation of $G$, so it is $C^*\ker\pi$ for some $\pi\in\widehat G$. The last assertion is the universal property of the quotient by the equivalence relation $\pi\sim\rho\Leftrightarrow C^*\ker\pi=C^*\ker\rho$ (the Kolmogorov quotient of the dual, [BeH–19, §1.E]); its identification with $\operatorname{Prim}(C^*(G))$ with the Jacobson topology is exactly [[thm-the-kernel-map-is-a-homeomorphism-onto-the-primitive-ideal-space]].

items.title: Full and reduced group C star algebras of a finite group
items.statement: Assume AC. Let $G$ be a finite group. Then $C^*(G)=C^*_r(G)$ as C*-algebras, and both are $*$-isomorphic to the finite-dimensional semisimple algebra $\bigoplus_{\pi\in\widehat G}\operatorname{End}(H_\pi)\cong\bigoplus_{\pi\in\widehat G}M_{d_\pi}(\mathbb C)$, where $d_\pi=\dim H_\pi$.
items.strategy: A finite group is compact, so every irreducible unitary representation is finite dimensional and every unitary representation is a discrete direct sum of irreducibles ([[thm-arbitrary-unitary-representations-of-compact-groups-decompose-discretely]], [[def-unitary-dual-of-a-compact-group]]); the left regular representation contains every irreducible class ([[thm-l2-peter-weyl-orthonormal-basis]]), so the full norm and the reduced norm agree and $C^*(G)=C^*_r(G)$. The integrated forms identify this algebra with the image of $L^1(G)=\mathbb C[G]$ in $\bigoplus_\pi\operatorname{End}(H_\pi)$; the map is injective because the regular representation is faithful, and dimension count ($|G|=\sum_\pi d_\pi^2$) makes it surjective. The universal property is that of [[thm-nondegenerate-representations-of-c-star-g-are-unitary-representations-of-g]]. AC is declared and inherited from [[thm-unitary-representations-and-nondegenerate-l1-star-representations-correspond]], which assumes it; the dependency is declared as [[def-axiom-of-choice]].

items.title: Unitary dual and full group C star algebra of the integers
items.statement: Assume AC. For $G=\mathbb Z$, $\widehat{\mathbb Z}$ is the circle group $\mathbb T$ of continuous characters $\chi_z(n)=z^n$, $C^*(\mathbb Z)\cong C(\mathbb T)$, and $C^*_r(\mathbb Z)\cong C(\mathbb T)$ as well; the isomorphism sends $\delta_1$ to the function $z\mapsto z$.
items.strategy: The dual of a discrete abelian group is the compact character group with the compact-open topology, and for $\mathbb Z$ evaluation at $1$ identifies it with $\mathbb T$ ([[def-pontryagin-dual-and-compact-open-topology]], [[thm-compact-groups-have-discrete-duals-and-discrete-groups-have-compact-duals]]). The Gelfand transform of $L^1(\mathbb Z)=\ell^1(\mathbb Z)$ is the Fourier transform onto a dense subalgebra of $C(\mathbb T)$ ([[ex-gelfand-transform-of-l-one-of-an-lca-group]]), and $C^*(\mathbb Z)\cong C(\widehat{\mathbb Z})\cong C(\mathbb T)$ by [[cor-the-abelian-group-c-star-algebra-recovers-pontryagin-duality]] with [[thm-locally-compact-gelfand-duality]]. Since $\mathbb Z$ is amenable every representation is weakly contained in the regular representation, so the full and reduced norms and algebras coincide; the element $\delta_1$ acts as the function $z\mapsto z$. AC is declared and inherited from [[cor-the-abelian-group-c-star-algebra-recovers-pontryagin-duality]], which assumes it; the dependency is declared as [[def-axiom-of-choice]].

items.title: Fell convergence of the characters of the real line
items.statement: Assume AC. For $G=\mathbb R$, the unitary dual is $\{\chi_t:t\in\mathbb R\}$ with $\chi_t(x)=e^{itx}$, and a net $\chi_{t_i}$ converges to $\chi_t$ in the Fell topology if and only if $t_i\to t$ in $\mathbb R$; moreover $\chi_{t_i}\prec\chi_t$ for every $t_i$, $t$, so weak containment between characters carries no information beyond the Fell topology of the circle parametrisation.
items.strategy: Characters of $\mathbb R$ are the exponentials $x\mapsto e^{itx}$ ([[lem-continuous-characters-of-the-real-line-are-exponentials]]) and the compact-open topology on them is the usual topology of $\mathbb R$ ([[def-pontryagin-dual-and-compact-open-topology]]). For the Fell topology: a character is one dimensional, so its functions of positive type are the constants $c\cdot1$ for the trivial character and $c|\chi_t|$-multiples of $\chi_t$; unwinding the Fell basis of [[def-fell-topology-on-the-unitary-dual]] shows that $\chi_{t_i}\to\chi_t$ iff $\chi_{t_i}\to\chi_t$ uniformly on compact subsets of $\mathbb R$, which holds iff $t_i\to t$ by joint continuity of $(t,x)\mapsto e^{itx}$ and compactness. Weak containment of characters is convergence in the Fell topology by [[lem-fell-closure-of-a-single-representation-is-its-weak-containment-closure]]. AC is declared and inherited from [[def-fell-topology-on-the-unitary-dual]], which assumes it; the dependency is declared as [[def-axiom-of-choice]].

items.title: The unitary dual need not be Hausdorff
items.statement: Assume AC. There is a second-countable locally compact group whose unitary dual, with the Fell topology, is not Hausdorff. Explicitly, let $G=\mathbb R_{>0}\ltimes\mathbb R$ be the affine group of the line, with $(a,b)(a',b')=(aa',b+ab')$ and the topology of $\mathbb R_{>0}\times\mathbb R$, and let $\pi$ be the representation on $L^2(\mathbb R)$ given by $(\pi(a,b)\eta)(u)=e^{ibe^u}\eta(u+\log a)$. Then: (1) $\pi$ is a strongly continuous irreducible unitary representation and $\pi\not\simeq1_G$ (it is infinite dimensional); (2) every unitary character $\chi_t(a,b)=a^{it}$ ($t\in\mathbb R$) lies in the Fell closure of the singleton $\{\pi\}$, so in particular the trivial character $1_G=\chi_0$ does; (3) hence the singleton $\{\pi\}$ is not closed and $\widehat G$ is not a Hausdorff space. This is the source's non-type-I example ([BeHV–08, Example F.2.5(iii)], after [Fell–62, §5]); the source also records the full enumeration $\widehat G=\{\chi_t:t\in\mathbb R\}\cup\{\pi\}$, which is not used here.
items.strategy: The group is a locally compact second-countable semidirect product ([[def-external-semidirect-product]], [[def-topological-group]]). Unitarity of $\pi$ is the change of variables $u\mapsto u+\log a$ in $L^2(\mathbb R)$; multiplicativity is the cocycle identity $(a,b)(a',b')=(aa',b+ab')$; strong continuity follows from continuity of translations in $L^2$ and dominated convergence applied to the phase factor $e^{ibe^u}-e^{ib_0e^u}$. Irreducibility: an operator $T$ commuting with $\pi$ commutes with the multiplications by $e^{ibe^u}$, $b\in\mathbb R$ ([[lem-operators-commuting-with-a-point-separating-family-of-multiplications-are-multiplications]]), so $T=M_m$; commuting with the dilations $\pi(a,0)$ forces $m(u+\log a)=m(u)$ a.e. for every $a>0$, hence $m$ is a.e. constant and $T$ is scalar; the scalar-commutant form of Schur's lemma ([[thm-schurs-lemma-for-unitary-representations]]) gives irreducibility. Since $\pi$ acts on $L^2(\mathbb R)$, it is infinite dimensional, so $\pi\not\simeq1_G$. Characters in the closure: fix $t\in\mathbb R$, $R>1$ and let $\eta_R(u)=(R/2)^{-1/2}e^{itu}\mathbf 1_{[-R,-R/2]}(u)$, a unit vector. For $(a,b)\in G$ with $|\log a|\le L$ and $|b|\le B$ one computes $\langle\pi(a,b)\eta_R,\eta_R\rangle=a^{it}\int e^{ibe^u}|g_R(u+\log a)|\,|g_R(u)|\,du$, where $g_R=(R/2)^{-1/2}\mathbf 1_{[-R,-R/2]}$, because the phase $e^{itu}$ compensates the shift by $\log a$; hence the coefficient is within $Be^{L-R/2}$ of $\chi_t(a,b)=a^{it}$ uniformly on that compact set. Thus $\chi_t\prec\pi$, and by [[lem-fell-closure-of-a-single-representation-is-its-weak-containment-closure]] $\chi_t$ lies in the Fell closure of $\{\pi\}$. Finally, if $\widehat G$ were Hausdorff, the point $1_G=\chi_0$ would be closed, contradicting $1_G\in\overline{\{\pi\}}$ with $\pi\neq1_G$. AC is inherited from [[def-fell-topology-on-the-unitary-dual]].
